A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoVT/AdaVaR research. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of AdaVaR-3B and AdaVaR-7B, ablation experiments, training dynamics, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on sensitivity, robustness, computational efficiency, and mode-selection behavior.

M1.justification: The two-stage SFT/AdaGRPO procedure, reasoning modes, prefix-guided exploration, advantages, rewards, and curriculum remain unchanged. The expanded scalability discussion concerns prospective extensions; newly documented implementation details do not establish a changed implemented method.

E1.justification: The training corpora and eight benchmark tasks are retained. Appendix C.7.5 adds evaluation with Gaussian-blurred images, introducing a limited degraded-input scenario. New MMStar subgroup analyses and examples use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set is unchanged. v2 Table 6 adds Expert Pick and Max(GRD, TXT), two dataset-level mode-selection strategies compared against AdaVaR's adaptive selection.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial controlled evaluation protocols: fixed-total SFT mixtures at 1:1, 3:1, and 1:3 ratios; alternate prefixes and training/evaluation prompts; omission of SFT; reversed curriculum order; and Gaussian blur with radius 0.5. It also specifies attention aggregation and computational profiling protocols, including timing averaged over 100 training steps. Existing benchmark splits and principal training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing ablations, v2 tests dependence on data balance, prefix semantics, SFT, prompt descriptions, curriculum order, and image quality. It adds attention and image-type analyses, selection-versus-reasoning error breakdowns, efficiency comparisons, supplementary training curves, and two MMStar cases. These substantially broaden scrutiny of the method.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or evaluation seed information. v2's 100-step timing average is a new measurement protocol, without accompanying uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation values are retained, including v1 Table 5 as v2 Table 7. Substantial new results include average accuracies of 49.8 for Expert Pick and 50.1 for Max(GRD, TXT), 46.5 without SFT, 50.0 with reversed curriculum, and 50.5 under blur, compared with the retained AdaVaR-3B average of 50.8. New attention, error, efficiency, and qualitative findings further expand the results.

T1.justification: The probability factorization, Gaussian reward assumptions, mode-advantage derivation, and optimization objectives are unchanged. Algorithm 1 clarifies the reward-array inputs without changing its calculation. No new formal theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: unified reasoning modes, context-adaptive selection through AdaVaR/AdaGRPO, and broad benchmark improvements. The claims that AdaVaR-3B approaches Qwen2.5-VL-7B and AdaVaR-7B surpasses GPT-4o on average are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of text-dominated mode-selection attention, sample-level complementarity, selection errors, prompt sensitivity, SFT dependence, and computational cost. It expands future-work discussion into width/depth extensions and identifies limited multilingual training/evaluation data as an applicability constraint. These go substantially beyond v1's existing mode-complementarity and future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised artifact release with a repository link and a statement that code, data, and weights are available. It adds preprocessing, licensing and data-quality checks, the 8192-token mode-switching threshold, benchmark averaging rules, checkpoint/evaluation instructions, vLLM hardware details, and KV-cache sharing information. These expand reproducibility disclosure without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting implementation and analysis, including R1-V, VLM-R1, Open R1, Kaduri et al.'s attention analysis, and Kwon et al.'s serving framework. The main related-work positioning is retained. Changing the DeepSeek-R1 citation from DeepSeek-AI to Guo et al. identifies the same work.

P1.justification: v2 adds an appendix roadmap, finer subsection organization, and expanded implementation and future-work explanations. Affiliations, publication headers, acknowledgments, and cross-references are updated. The main narrative and much of the retained appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with comparison, error, efficiency, and sensitivity tables; attention distributions and heatmaps; training curves; an extension diagram; and additional qualitative cases. Existing displays are retained, including v1 Table 5 becoming Table 7 and Figures 7–11 becoming Figures 11–15. New Table 6 incorrectly reverses the POPE and V* headings relative to the retained results.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method: Appendix C.7 directly tests whether its behavior depends on prompt wording, prefix semantics, SFT, and data balance, while the error and efficiency analyses clarify practical strengths and weaknesses. Expanded reproducibility information further improves auditability. These gains outweigh localized new reporting errors, notably Table 6's swapped POPE/V* headings and Table 11's overhead wording contradicting its timing values.
